evidence_quotes.quote: The simplicity of the Environmental Kuznets (EKC) curve concept motivated this study of the relationships between environmental, economic and social indicators at the country, city/regional and manufacturing facility scale.
this study uses country-scale GDP (Purchasing Price Parity-adjusted) for country scale analysis and experiments with using city/regional GDP at the local scale.

Surprising results are shown for life expectancy and access to improved water and sanitation systems. While all generally increase with increasing GDP, the relationships are not monotonic -- meaning there is unexpected curvature in the patterns.

raw_response.plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both narrow and plain readings of Criterion 2 because the exposure is purely macroeconomic wealth (GDP per capita and corporate market maturity in an Environmental Kuznets Curve framework) with no legal, administrative, regulatory, institutional, or governance factor examined.
raw_response.rationale: Although this empirical dissertation includes country-scale access to improved water and sanitation systems among eight environmental and social indicators (meeting Criteria 1, 3, and 4), its explanatory variable is strictly macroeconomic income/wealth (PPP-adjusted GDP at country and city/regional scales and a corporate market-maturity metric for Coca-Cola manufacturing facilities) testing the Environmental Kuznets Curve hypothesis. No legal, administrative, regulatory, or institutional mechanism governing water or sanitation access is examined (E03).
